produkt.dna_utdrag:
PRODUCT FACTS (only these): IBC tank cover for a standard 1000-litre IBC tank. Green 210D Oxford fabric (210D — never 220D). Zipper along the side: on and off without tools, no tarp, no rubber bands. Opening at the top so the lid is reachable without taking the cover off. Size 120 × 100 × 116 cm. Fits on in under two minutes. Drawstrings at the bottom hold it in place. Delivery 6–10 working days, free shipping within Sweden. 14 days right of withdrawal (never '30 dagars öppet köp'). Brand: TankGuard (capital T, capital G). Landing page https://tankguard.se/products/tankoverdraget.

MECHANISM (the thing that sells): sunlight straight into the tank makes algae grow in the water, and UV makes the plastic brittle year by year. The fabric takes the sun instead of the plastic, and without light the algae never get started. Light is the cause, not the water.

CUSTOMER: villa, summer-house and allotment owners 35–70 who collect rainwater in an IBC tank for the garden. They already know the water turns green; they do not know it is the light that does it. The problem in the order they feel it: 1) water turns green with algae — visible, smells, cannot water with it; 2) the scrubbing, every summer; 3) the plastic goes brittle in UV — slow, invisible, it is what kills the tank.

SOCIAL PROOF WE ACTUALLY HAVE: 16 reviews on tankguard.se (verified live 2026-09-12). Verbatim reviews you may quote WITH first name only: Anders: "Väldigt bra överdrag. Passar min IBC-tank perfekt och är enkelt att sätta på." · Lena: "Köpte detta för min regnvattentank. Fungerar bra och är enkelt att öppna när jag behöver." · Sofia: "Passar bra på tanken och skyddar mot solen. Precis vad jag behövde." · Magnus: "Bra material och känns stabilt. Lätt att montera på tanken." Never invent other customers, counts or star averages.

INHERITED WINNING LINES (spent money well on the source store, same product): primary-text opener "Trött på grönt, algfyllt regnvatten?" (16 997 kr, 77 purchases behind it). Script lines from the winning film: "Solen gör plasten spröd och vattnet blir grönt av alger." · "Ett skyddsöverdrag i kraftigt 210D Oxfordtyg. Det blockerar solljus och UV-strålar helt." · "Installationen tar två minuter. Dra ner blixtlåset. Klart!" · "Du behöver inte ta av överdraget för att kolla vattnet. Det finns en öppning upptill rakt över locket." · "Klart vatten, ingen algtillväxt och en tank som håller längre." Product-page problem line: "Presenningen som skulle skydda blåser av vid första höststormen."

SEASON: it is September. Frost and autumn storms are coming; the tank stands outside all winter. Urgency may come from the season only — never from stock, price changes or 'bara idag'.

briefer.hypotes: Same inherited PD_1 film as PD_7_H1. Hypothesis: opening with the CAUSE the customer does not know (it is the light, not the water) stops the scroll better than opening with the problem they already know. The product page that converted 86 purchases on the source store leads with exactly this: light is the cause.

briefer.hook_ide: It is not the water that is the problem. It is the light. (max 8 Swedish words; a flat claim, no question)
briefer.format: Video ~30 s, 9:16. Same film as PD_7_H1 and the inherited PD_1. Only the first 3 seconds change.
briefer.kept: Everything from 0:03 onward is the inherited PD_1 script, verbatim, in this order: PROBLEM "Har du en IBC-tank för regnvatten? Då vet du problemet. Solen gör plasten spröd och vattnet blir grönt av alger." · MEKANISM "Det här är lösningen. Ett skyddsöverdrag i kraftigt 210D Oxfordtyg. Det blockerar solljus och UV-strålar helt. Klart vatten, ingen algtillväxt och en tank som håller längre." · CTA "Ett IBC-tanköverdrag från TankGuard. 489 kr." Reproduce these lines exactly as the manus beats PROBLEM/MEKANISM/PROOF/CTA — do not rewrite them.

briefer.format: Video 20–25 s, 9:16. New film: a tarp flapping / lifted off a tank by wind (or hands pulling it off), cut to the cover zipped on and the drawstrings pulled tight. No people in frame.
briefer.changed: New concept. Five beats. MEKANISM: zipper along the side + drawstrings at the bottom — this is why it stays on. PROOF: 210D Oxford fabric, the measurements, two minutes to fit.

briefer.hypotes: The product page (86 purchases on the source store) carries a second angle the ads never tested on its own: the tank ages in the sun, not in the water — 210D fabric takes the UV instead of the plastic. The winning film says it in one line ("Solen gör plasten spröd") but leads with algae. Hypothesis: for the customer who already lives with green water, the slow, invisible cost (the tank itself going brittle) is a stronger reason to buy than one more algae ad.
briefer.vinkel: UV — the plastic goes brittle in the sun; the fabric takes the sun instead
briefer.hook_ide: The sun is eating your tank, year by year — the fabric takes the sun instead of the plastic. (max 8 words; must be visualisable: plastic, sun, brittle)
briefer.format: Video 20–25 s, 9:16. New film: close-up of sun on bare IBC plastic (chalky, faded), then the green fabric going over it. Hands only.
briefer.kept: Price 489 kr in the CTA. Never claim a number of years or a lifespan — we have no measurement.
briefer.changed: New concept. Five beats. PROBLEM: UV makes the plastic brittle — slow and invisible until it cracks. MEKANISM: the fabric takes the sun instead of the plastic; without light the algae never start either (two problems, one cover).
